12faaa76365814de1195d6bdf1e5ba05.description: This is a screenshot of the Hexo project's homepage, a dark-themed site with a hexagonal "H" logo and a top nav for Docs, API, News, Plugins, Themes, and About. 13d5b6bcd2b0dce847951d4e3faf89ca.description: A photograph shows a dark-colored laptop, screen off and reflecting a rippled purplish sheen, perched open on top of a stone or concrete pillar overlooking a wide, muddy-brown river. 18dc4b33f21890aa9042955b67ac346d.description: This is a screenshot of an iPhone Settings screen showing the SIMs section, with two eSIM entries both toggled on: "Travel - CMHK" labeled T1, and "Travel - Hutchison HK" labeled T2, the latter displaying a partially blurred Hong Kong phone number starting with +852 51 and ending in 77. 2722532798307eb9c03d89e2343c2cda.description: A screenshot of a marketing landing page for a product called Typeless, with a bird-like logo and top navigation links for Manifesto, Pricing, and About, plus a black "Download for macOS" button in the corner. The large centered headline reads "Speak, don't type" in bold black-and-gray text, followed by a paragraph explaining that speaking naturally lets Typeless "turn your words into polished messages, emails, and documents" that read as if carefully typed, in real time, and "4x faster than typing." Below the text sits a second, pill-shaped black "Download for macOS" call-to-action button, centered on an otherwise plain white background. The page is evidence of a dictation-to-text macOS app being promoted with a speed and polish claim over traditional typing.

2acad555d6fe7cbcd5b153ce945585a0.description: A photograph taken along a paved footpath cutting through a park or residential courtyard, with weeds and grass sprouting through cracks in the worn concrete. Thick, somewhat overgrown shrubs and bamboo-like hedges line both sides, flanked by trees with white-painted trunks on the right and a leafless tree and a rusted, roofless metal pergola structure in the middle distance. Beyond a low fence and railing on the left stands a tan multi-story building, its windows partly obscured by bare branches, while soft, hazy daylight suggests an overcast morning or late afternoon. The neglected pavement and untrimmed vegetation suggest a lightly maintained green space within an older apartment complex or institutional compound.

3f34360a5eb3c9ec303ca1035cc2453b.description: A screenshot of the Bytecode Alliance's documentation page for Cranelift, with a top navigation bar linking to Documentation, API Reference, Contributing, Chat, and a GitHub icon. Below a large "Cranelift" heading, the body text describes it as a fast, secure, relatively simple, and innovative compiler backend written in Rust that compiles intermediate representations into executable machine code, used by the Wasmtime WebAssembly virtual machine for JIT and AOT compilation and experimentally as a Rust compiler backend. It goes on to state that Cranelift currently supports x86-64, aarch64 (ARM64), s390x (IBM Z), and riscv64 platforms, is retargetable, and welcomes further ISA contributions, and notes it is actively maintained for running sandboxed untrusted code with close-to-native performance, following Wasmtime's release and security policies. The page serves as evidence of Cranelift's project scope, supported architectures, and its role within the Bytecode Alliance ecosystem.

5104d3b6f735fbe76558681b4d37e8ce.description: A terminal screenshot shows the tail end of a Cargo build log for a Rust workspace called "seam", titled `~/C/P/seam` with the shell running under user `canmi` on branch `main`. Dozens of dependency crates compile in sequence (console, reqwest, clap, tokio-tungstenite, notify, indicatif, and others), followed by the project's own crates — seam-codegen, seam-server-axum, seam-skeleton, seam-injector-wasm, seam-engine-wasm, seam-cli, all at version 0.5.38 — and several example backends (github-dashboard-axum, i18n-demo-axum, markdown-demo-rust, demo-server-rust). 5898c4f0bf6412e9323eca7b85c75365.description: A photograph taken indoors, likely in a parking garage or utility corridor, showing a rough concrete wall with a wall-mounted fire hydrant cabinet on the left, labeled "消火栓 / FIRE HYDRANT" in red text on white, alongside exposed pipes and a small wall-mounted exhaust vent above it. Painted in dripping red characters across the lower band of the wall is the warning "消防通道严禁停车" (fire lane, parking strictly prohibited), the paint runs suggesting it was applied by hand with a brush or roller rather than printed. The bare concrete floor, unfinished walls, and utility fittings indicate this is a service or basement area where the sign serves as evidence of an active effort to keep the fire access route clear of parked vehicles.

5c33f853b73251e594e7c0eaca0a5709.description: This is a screenshot of the Next.js homepage, dark-themed with a triangular logo and a top nav listing Showcase, Docs, Blog, Templates, Enterprise, a search bar, and Deploy and Learn buttons. 6da637a66b48711354532477ac3f2014.description: This is a screenshot mockup promoting a blog theme, showing a "Nlvi" wordmark logo with a coral underline on the left, paired with two overlapping browser-window previews of a site built with the Hexo static-site generator. Both preview panes display the same demo post dated 2013-12-27, titled "Elements," with placeholder Lorem Ipsum text and a full stack of typographic samples: headings 1 through 6 in descending size, a paragraph section with styled links, bold and italic text, underlines, and a blockquote, followed by a three-column table with "Table Header 1/2/3" and "Division" rows. The top navigation bar reads "ARTICLE, ARCHIVES, TAGS, ABOUT" alongside a search icon, indicating this is a style-guide or theme-demo page meant to showcase how HTML elements render within the Hexo theme.

7d3a80a688fa627e4f3577f69b320867.description: This is a bar chart comparing link times across four linkers -- GNU ld 2.42, GNU gold 2.38, LLVM lld 19.0.0, and mold 2.4.0 -- on three programs of increasing binary size: MySQL 8.3 (0.47 GiB), Clang 19.0 (1.56 GiB), and Chromium 124 (1.35 GiB), with time to link in seconds on the vertical axis. GNU ld takes about 11 seconds on MySQL and roughly 42 seconds on Clang but has no bar for Chromium, GNU gold rises from about 7.5 seconds to 33 seconds to 27 seconds across the three, while LLVM lld and mold stay far lower throughout, with lld around 2, 5, and 6 seconds and mold consistently under 2 seconds. The chart is evidence that mold and LLVM lld scale far better with binary size than the traditional GNU ld and gold linkers, whose link times grow much more steeply as the program being linked gets larger.

8acf126a993024efcb5d4db159659d40.description: A screenshot of the Vercel marketing homepage on a black background, with a top navigation bar reading Products, Resources, Solutions, Enterprise, and Pricing, plus Ask AI, Log In, and Sign Up buttons beside the triangular Vercel logo. 8d32cfe9437f0bba72819263799a99ca.description: A photograph, taken outdoors looking straight down at a patch of lawn where green grass blades push up through a scattering of dry, brittle brown and beige leaves and thatch. A couple of curled reddish-brown leaves sit near the center of the frame, flanked by two thin pale twigs bending upward through the vegetation, with a bit of white plastic debris visible at the lower left edge. The lighting is soft and even, consistent with an overcast day or diffuse daylight, and the image reads as an unremarkable close-up snapshot of ground cover rather than a staged or documentary shot of anything in particular.

917811350fbfc7af291fce7bd549ef3e.description: A photograph taken along a weathered wooden boardwalk that runs beneath a series of rusted metal pergola frames, their trellis tops long since stripped of any climbing plants and left bare against the sky. Dense bamboo and overgrown shrubs crowd both sides of the path, their leaves catching daylight while the wood planks below show gaps, warping, and patches of moss or sprouting weeds pushing up between the boards. In the distance the walkway continues past bare-branched winter trees toward what looks like a pond or open clearing, with a cluster of residential high-rises visible above the greenery on the upper left. The overall impression is of an abandoned or neglected park walkway, reclaimed by vegetation after a period of disuse.

a10408f6aebb21591eed99bdacd7c1e5.description: A photograph taken from an elevated riverside promenade, looking out over a wide, calm expanse of grayish-brown river water under an overcast, hazy sky. Two street lamps and a metal railing line the foreground walkway, while a dense mat of dark floating debris or algae hugs the near shoreline, spreading out in an irregular band before giving way to open water. In the far distance, faint vertical reflections suggest the pillars of a bridge or elevated structure, with a small red-and-dark boat or buoy barely visible near the horizon. The murky water and drifting clutter near the shore point to poor water quality or accumulated pollution along this stretch of the river.

a46df6030a9b1ba3f0af95e1a2196850.description: It's a photograph taken outdoors, looking down at a low, dense hedge of small-leaved shrubs planted along a street or sidewalk, with a granite curb running diagonally from the lower left toward the upper right and a paved road visible in the bottom-left corner. The hedge shows fresh light-green new growth on darker woody branches, with a tree trunk base visible near the top edge and a strip of mulched or bare brown ground beyond the shrubs. a904d61e5006b602f7c6efd236911d78.description: A screenshot of a terminal or app window displaying a dark-themed data table titled with a truncated path ending in "roject," listing daily model usage across dated rows from 2026-03-03 to 2026-03-13, with columns for the models used (combinations of haiku-4-5, opus-4-6, and sonnet-4-6), several numeric usage columns growing into the billions, and a final dollar-cost column ranging from about $97.92 to $1,765.56 per day. cbc260f16e936f977570f8fb391f48e2.description: This is a screenshot of a terminal window titled "~/C/P/seam" showing the tail end of a `cargo build --release` run for a project called "seam." The scroll lists dozens of dependency crates compiling in sequence — walkdir, rand, tungstenite, sha2, toml, notify, rquickjs, clap and others — followed by the project's own workspace members such as seam-codegen, seam-skeleton, seam-injector-wasm, seam-engine-wasm, seam-server, seam-server-axum, seam-cli, and several example backends (demo-server-rust, github-dashboard-axum, markdown-demo-rust, i18n-demo-axum). The final lines confirm success: "Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 1m 05s," followed by an idle shell prompt reading `canmi@xyy ~/C/P/seam (main)>`. It is evidence of a clean, complete release build of a multi-crate Rust monorepo with WASM and Axum server components.
